run.database: ekgyjwoenteadaaqakmd (shared by CI E2E and production)
run.note: verification 'INSPECTION' = proven from live database catalog (pg_policies, grants) or source code; the exploit itself was not executed in this run.

defects.title: Any tenant member can write governance tables directly through PostgREST, bypassing RBAC, audit, validation and the SSRF guard
defects.test: pg_policies: 47 INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies on 25 tables whose only condition is tenant_id IN current_tenant_ids(). Live write probe as READ_ONLY was refused by the session permission classifier and not executed.
defects.evidence: Tables: access_requests, accounts, agent_identities, agent_owners, agent_relationships (DELETE), agents, applications, certification_campaigns, data_sources, entitlements, identities, identity_attribute_definitions, identity_lifecycle_events, identity_lifecycle_tasks, identity_relationships, identity_sources, integration_mappings, integration_sync_jobs, integrations, policies, policy_exceptions, policy_rules, policy_versions, reports, risk_severity_weights. Table privileges INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE granted to authenticated. No guarding triggers on agents, integrations, policies, risk_severity_weights.
defects.impact: A READ_ONLY/REQUESTER/AUDITOR user signs in with their own password plus the public publishable key and can: reactivate a suspended agent or change lifecycle_state (agents.status), disable or soften policies (policies.status/action), zero risk weights, insert policy_exceptions, file access_requests with forged requested_by/policy_result/risk_level, and rewrite integrations.config.baseUrl/capabilities. The next sync then sends the decrypted connector secret to an attacker-chosen host, bypassing the SSRF guard and the read-only capability rule (non-negotiables #10, #12). None of these writes produce an audit event (#11).
sourceFiles: supabase/migrations (RLS policies for the tables above)
defects.suggestedFix: Drop the client INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies on these tables (writes already go through server services, most with the service role), or gate each with has_tenant_permission(tenant_id, '<module>.manage'). Then revoke UPDATE(tenant_id) from authenticated. Add the live probe (READ_ONLY write attempts must affect 0 rows) to the QA suite against a non-production database.

defects.title: A member of two organizations can move rows between them by updating tenant_id
defects.test: has_column_privilege('authenticated', <table>, 'tenant_id', 'UPDATE') = true for agents, policies, integrations, identities, access_requests, policy_exceptions, risk_severity_weights, agent_relationships; UPDATE WITH CHECK only requires the new tenant_id to be one of the caller's tenants.
defects.evidence: Same policy set as E2E-001. Composite same-tenant foreign keys (migration 0076) block moving a row that has cross-referenced children, but leaf rows are not protected.
defects.impact: Cross-tenant data movement (exfiltration from org A into org B where the user is an admin) by a user who holds only READ_ONLY in org A. Rated HIGH, not CRITICAL, because it requires membership in both organizations; upgrade to CRITICAL if confirmed live.
defects.suggestedFix: Revoke UPDATE on tenant_id from authenticated on every tenant table (or add a BEFORE UPDATE trigger raising when NEW.tenant_id <> OLD.tenant_id). Confirm with a rolled-back SQL fixture using a two-membership user.

defects.title: Role assignment and group membership have no privilege ceiling
defects.test: Code review of assignRole() and addGroupMember().
defects.evidence: lib/rbac/roles.ts:118 assignRole() checks only actorId !== targetUserId, role exists and is active. lib/users/groups.ts:318 addGroupMember() needs only groups.manage_members and checks only actorId !== userId. Custom-role design (lib/rbac/customRoles.ts escalationIn) does enforce a ceiling, so the gap is specific to assignment.
defects.impact: A delegated administrator holding a custom role with roles.assign can grant TENANT_SUPER_ADMIN to a colleague or to a second account they invited (users.invite). A holder of groups.manage_members, without roles.assign, can add anyone to a group that carries TENANT_SUPER_ADMIN.
defects.suggestedFix: Before assigning a role (directly, through invite, or by adding a member to a group with roles), require that the actor holds every permission of each role being conferred (reuse escalationIn from lib/rbac/roleRules.ts). Treat adding a member to a group with roles as role assignment (require roles.assign).

defects.title: Open redirect in /auth/callback via backslash in ?next=
defects.test: node: isSafeRelativeNextPath('/\\evil.example') === true; new URL('/\\evil.example', 'https://agent.wonderapps.biz/auth/callback').href === 'https://evil.example/'. The same holds for '/\t/evil.example'.
defects.evidence: app/auth/callback/route.ts:15-17 accepts any value starting with '/' and not '//'.
defects.impact: After a successful code exchange the user is redirected off-site (phishing after a genuine sign-in or password reset).
defects.suggestedFix: Resolve with new URL(next, request.url) and require result.origin === new URL(request.url).origin; also reject backslashes and control characters.

defects.title: Idle and absolute session timeouts rely on client-held cookies that can be dropped to reset the clock
defects.test: proxy.ts: when wa_session_started_at is absent it is backfilled to now; checkSessionExpiry(null, null) is never expired.
defects.impact: A client (or a stolen-token replay through curl) that omits the two cookies is never idle- or absolute-expired by the app. Supabase JWT and refresh-token lifetimes still apply.
defects.suggestedFix: Anchor the absolute timeout to the session's server-side creation time (JWT iat / auth.sessions.created_at) and the idle timeout to a server-side last-seen record, not to client cookies.

defects.title: Users can rewrite their own public.users email and display_name directly
defects.test: Policy users_update_self: USING/WITH CHECK id = auth.uid(), no column restriction; UPDATE granted to authenticated.
defects.evidence: public.users has columns id, email, display_name, created_at. Admin screens, group/role holder lists and email notifications (modules/operations/email.ts:97) read these columns.
defects.impact: A user can impersonate another person's name or email in approval queues, holder lists and audit displays, and silently redirect their own notifications.
defects.suggestedFix: Restrict the self-update policy to display_name via column grants (REVOKE UPDATE(email)), and keep email synced only from auth.users.

defects.title: SSO JIT role resolution lets user_metadata override IdP claims
defects.test: app/auth/callback/route.ts merges claims as { ...identityData, ...user.user_metadata }; resolveJitRole reads the configured role claim from the merged object.
defects.evidence: user_metadata is writable by the user via supabase.auth.updateUser({ data }).
defects.impact: If an account's user_metadata carries the configured role claim before JIT provisioning, the self-asserted value outranks the IdP's. Exploitability depends on GoTrue's SSO sign-in behaviour; needs a test IdP to confirm.
defects.suggestedFix: Read role/group claims only from the IdP-asserted identity_data (or app_metadata), never from user_metadata.

defects.title: Certification 'delegate' accepts any user id
defects.test: Code review of recordDecision delegate branch.
defects.evidence: modules/certification-compliance/decisions.ts:39-40 only checks presence; :187 writes reviewer_id = delegateToUserId with the service role. There is no check that the delegate is an active member of the tenant or not an owner of the reviewed agent.
defects.impact: A reviewer can hand an item to a non-member (the item becomes unreviewable) or to the agent's own owner, steering it toward self-certification (the owner still meets the SoD prompt at decision time).
defects.suggestedFix: Validate that delegateToUserId is an active member of the tenant with compliance.decide and is not an owner of the item's agent.

defects.title: Webhook receiver has no replay window and echoes database errors
defects.evidence: modules/integrations/webhooks.ts: the HMAC covers the body only (no timestamp). Bodies without id/eventId get randomUUID(), so a replayed signed body creates a new row each time. An upsert error returns insertError.message to the caller.
defects.impact: Replay of captured signed bodies creates duplicate activity rows; internal error text is visible to the caller.
defects.suggestedFix: Sign a timestamp header with the body and reject outside a replay window (reuse isWithinReplayWindow); derive a deterministic id from the body hash; return a generic error.

defects.title: Five routes validate input before authenticating
defects.test: Anonymous POST with an empty body: /api/v1/authorization-policies/[id]/status, /api/v1/roles/[id]/status, /api/v1/users/[id]/roles (POST and DELETE), /api/v1/users/[id]/status return 400 with schema hints; with a valid body they return 401.
defects.evidence: curl output recorded in E2E_TEST_EXECUTION.md phase 5.
defects.impact: Minor: an anonymous caller learns the expected input shape.
defects.suggestedFix: Resolve tenant context and permission before parsing the body.

defects.title: npm run typecheck fails on a fresh clone
defects.test: Fresh clone + npm ci + npm run typecheck → 8 × TS2307 for the PNG imports in app/welcome/page.tsx; passes after npx next typegen.
defects.evidence: next-env.d.ts is gitignored and generated only by next dev/build/typegen.
defects.impact: Typecheck as the first verification step in a new session or CI job without a build fails spuriously.

defects.title: Live isolation fixture drift and leftover SQL fixture tenants
defects.test: node tests/live-client-tenant-isolation.mjs → 150 PASS, 1 FAIL ('applications visible to B — 0 rows').
defects.evidence: e2e-tenant-two has 0 applications, so the reality check cannot prove isolation for that table. Tenants fixture-tenant-a5-test/b5-test remain in the shared database from an earlier SQL fixture run.
defects.impact: One table's isolation is unproven in that direction; stale fixture rows accumulate in a database that also serves production.
defects.suggestedFix: Seed one application in Tenant Two in seedTestData(); clean up the a5/b5 fixtures.

defects.title: E2E suite, SQL fixtures and production share one Supabase project
defects.test: Vercel production env NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL = project ekgyjwoenteadaaqakmd, the project the CI workflow and playwright.config.ts target; real tenants (e.g. Northwind Financial) live beside e2e-* tenants.
defects.impact: Every CI run writes test data into production. A test defect, a fixture cleanup bug or a mis-scoped query can touch customer tenants. Destructive and exploit-style security tests cannot be run safely, which is why E2E-001/002 could not be confirmed live.
defects.suggestedFix: Point CI and E2E at a separate Supabase project or a Supabase branch, and keep production secrets out of CI.

defects.title: Anonymous tenant enumeration through resolve_tenant_host
defects.test: resolve_tenant_host(p_subdomain, p_hostname) is SECURITY DEFINER and executable by anon; returns id, name, slug, status.
defects.evidence: Function source in the live database.
defects.impact: Anyone can confirm an organization's existence and learn its UUID, display name and status from a guessed slug.
defects.suggestedFix: Return only a boolean (the proxy uses only existence), or call it with the service role from the proxy.
